stem: A 0.2 kg ball strikes a wall at 10 m/s and rebounds along the same line at 10 m/s. The magnitude of the impulse on the ball is
explanation: Taking the rebound as negative, Δp = 0.2 × (10 − (−10)) = 4 N·s. A common slip is to subtract the speeds and get zero, forgetting that velocity reverses.

stem: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal force on the body is directed
options: towards the centre of the circle
explanation: The force changing the direction of velocity must point inwards. Away from the centre describes the so-called centrifugal effect, which is not a real force in an inertial frame.

stem: A motor lifts a 60 kg load through 20 m in 40 s at constant speed. Taking g = 10 m/s², its useful power output is
explanation: Work = mgh = 60 × 10 × 20 = 12,000 J, and P = W/t = 12,000/40 = 300 W. 12,000 is the work, not the power.

stem: For a projectile launched at an angle on level ground, the range is greatest, for a fixed launch speed and no air resistance, when the angle is
explanation: R = u² sin2θ/g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, that is θ = 45°. At 90° the projectile goes straight up and its range is zero.

stem: A wheel rotates at 120 revolutions per minute. Its angular speed in rad/s is
explanation: 120 rev/min = 2 rev/s, and each revolution is 2π rad, so ω = 4π rad/s. 240π results from multiplying by 2π without dividing by 60.

stem: Kepler's second law, that a line joining a planet to the Sun sweeps out equal areas in equal times, is a consequence of the conservation of
explanation: The Sun's pull is central, so it exerts no torque about the Sun, and the planet's angular momentum is constant. The planet therefore moves faster when nearer to the Sun.

stem: A force of 50 N pulls a trolley 10 m along the ground, with the force making an angle of 60° with the direction of motion. The work done is
explanation: W = Fd cosθ = 50 × 10 × 0.5 = 250 J. 500 J ignores the angle, and 433 J uses sin60° instead of cos60°.

stem: The surface escape speed of a planet is v. A second planet has the same radius but four times the mass. Its escape speed is
explanation: vₑ = √(2GM/R) ∝ √M at fixed radius, so quadrupling the mass doubles vₑ. The speed is not proportional to M itself.

stem: Which one of the following is a vector quantity?
explanation: Displacement has magnitude and direction. Work, speed and power are scalars; speed is only the magnitude of velocity.

stem: Two vectors have magnitudes 4 and 5 and the angle between them is 30°. The magnitude of their vector product is
explanation: |A × B| = AB sinθ = 4 × 5 × ½ = 10. 17.3 comes from using cos30°, which gives the scalar product.

stem: According to Bernoulli's principle, in a horizontal pipe carrying an ideal fluid, the pressure is lowest where
explanation: P + ½ρv² is constant along a streamline, so a higher speed means a lower pressure. The narrow section of a pipe has the highest speed.

stem: One watt is equal to
explanation: Power = energy/time, so 1 W = 1 J/s. A newton metre is also a joule, but that is energy, not power.

stem: The slope of a velocity–time graph at any instant gives the body's
explanation: Slope = Δv/Δt, which is acceleration. Displacement is the area under the graph, not its slope.

stem: A 0.5 kg stone is whirled in a horizontal circle of radius 2 m at a constant speed of 4 m/s. The tension in the string is
explanation: T = mv²/r = 0.5 × 16/2 = 4 N. Using mv² without dividing by r gives 8 N, and using mv/r gives 1 N.

stem: A car accelerates uniformly from 10 m/s to 30 m/s in 5 s. What is its acceleration?
explanation: a = (v − u)/t = (30 − 10)/5 = 4 m/s². Adding the speeds (40/5 = 8) is the common slip; acceleration depends on the change in velocity.

stem: For the same two surfaces, the limiting static friction compared with the kinetic friction is generally
explanation: It takes a larger force to start a body moving than to keep it moving, so μₛ > μₖ.

stem: The gauge pressure at a depth of 5 m in fresh water of density 1,000 kg/m³ is (g = 10 m/s²)
explanation: P = ρgh = 1,000 × 10 × 5 = 50,000 Pa. Leaving out g gives 5,000, and adding atmospheric pressure is not part of gauge pressure.

stem: What is the kinetic energy of a 2 kg object moving at 6 m/s?
explanation: KE = ½mv² = ½ × 2 × 36 = 36 J. Omitting the square gives 6 J and omitting the ½ gives 72 J.

stem: A force of 20 N acts perpendicular to a spanner at a distance of 0.3 m from the nut. The torque about the nut is
explanation: τ = rF sinθ = 0.3 × 20 × 1 = 6 N·m. 60 N·m comes from a decimal-place slip, and 0.015 from dividing the distance by the force.

stem: A small steel ball falls through a viscous liquid and reaches terminal velocity. At that stage
options: the ball has stopped accelerating because gravity vanishes
the viscous force is less than the weight
the net force on the ball is zero
explanation: At terminal speed, weight = upthrust + viscous drag, so the net force is zero and the speed is constant. Gravity continues to act.

stem: A moving ball collides head-on elastically with an identical ball at rest. Afterwards
options: the first ball stops and the second moves with the first ball's original velocity
both balls move with half the original velocity
the first ball continues at the same velocity
explanation: For equal masses in a head-on elastic collision, velocities are exchanged. Conserving both momentum and kinetic energy rules out the other outcomes.

stem: A skater spinning at 2 rad/s with moment of inertia 4 kg·m² pulls in her arms so that her moment of inertia becomes 1 kg·m². Her new angular speed is
explanation: Angular momentum is conserved: 4 × 2 = 1 × ω, so ω = 8 rad/s. Reducing I raises ω, so 0.5 rad/s (the inverted ratio) cannot be right.

stem: A rocket moves forward because
options: the exhaust pushes against the surrounding air
the exhaust gases carry momentum backwards, so the rocket gains equal momentum forward
its engine reduces its mass only
explanation: It is momentum conservation (equivalent to Newton's third law), which is why rockets work in vacuum, where there is no air to push against.

stem: A 2 kg trolley moving at 3 m/s collides with a 4 kg trolley at rest and they stick together. Their common speed is
explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 × 3 = (2 + 4)v, so v = 1 m/s. Using only the 2 kg mass in the denominator gives 3 m/s, which would mean no change.

stem: The escape velocity of an object from the Earth's surface depends on
options: the mass and radius of the Earth, but not on the mass of the object
the direction in which it is launched
explanation: vₑ = √(2GM/R) contains no term for the object's own mass.

stem: A satellite A orbits a planet at radius r and satellite B at radius 4r. The ratio of the period of B to that of A is
explanation: Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³, so T ∝ r^(3/2) = 4^(3/2) = 8. Ratios of 4 or 2 come from using T ∝ r or T ∝ √r.

stem: A passenger standing in a bus is thrown forward when the bus brakes suddenly. This is best explained by
explanation: The passenger tends to keep moving at the earlier velocity, which is inertia. The third law concerns action and reaction pairs acting on different bodies.

stem: A body starts with a speed of 5 m/s and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 4 s. How far does it travel?
explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 5(4) + ½(2)(16) = 20 + 16 = 36 m. Omitting the ½ gives 52 m, and using only ut gives 20 m.

stem: The orbital speed of a satellite in a circular orbit around the Earth is independent of
explanation: Equating GMm/r² to mv²/r, the satellite mass m cancels, leaving v = √(GM/r).

stem: The acceleration due to gravity on the Earth's surface is 10 m/s². At a height equal to the Earth's radius above the surface it is
explanation: The distance from the centre is 2R, and g ∝ 1/r², so g′ = 10/4 = 2.5 m/s². Halving (5 m/s²) wrongly treats g as ∝ 1/r.

stem: A satellite moves in a circular orbit around the Earth. The work done on it by the gravitational force during one revolution is
options: positive and equal to its kinetic energy
negative and equal to its potential energy
equal to mg times the orbital radius
explanation: The gravitational force always acts at 90° to the displacement, so W = Fd cos90° = 0. This is why the orbital speed stays constant.

stem: A ball is dropped from rest from a height of 20 m. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², its speed on reaching the ground is
explanation: mgh = ½mv² gives v = √(2gh) = √400 = 20 m/s. Leaving out the factor 2 gives √200 ≈ 14 m/s.

stem: The moment of inertia of a rigid body about an axis depends on
options: its mass distribution relative to the axis
explanation: I = Σmr², so the same body has different values for different axes. It is a property of the body and axis, not of the motion.

stem: In a hydraulic press the small piston has an area of 2 cm² and the large piston 100 cm². A force of 100 N acts on the small piston. The force on the large piston is
explanation: Pressure is transmitted equally: F₂ = F₁(A₂/A₁) = 100 × 50 = 5,000 N. Inverting the ratio would give only 2 N, and 200 N results from multiplying by the small area instead of dividing.

stem: A uniform seesaw has a girl of mass 40 kg sitting 1.5 m from the pivot. A boy sits on the other side, 2 m from the pivot, and it balances. The boy's mass is
explanation: Equal torques: 40 × 1.5 = m × 2, so m = 30 kg. Inverting the distances gives 53 kg.

stem: Masses of 3 kg and 5 kg hang from the two ends of a light string over a smooth light pulley. Taking g = 10 m/s², the acceleration of the masses is
explanation: a = (m₂ − m₁)g/(m₁ + m₂) = (2 × 10)/8 = 2.5 m/s². Dividing by only one mass, or forgetting to add the masses in the denominator, gives wrong values such as 5 m/s².

stem: A ball is projected at 30 m/s at 45° to the horizontal on level ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its horizontal range?
explanation: R = u² sin2θ/g = 900 × sin 90°/10 = 90 m. Using sinθ in place of sin2θ gives about 64 m, and 180 m results from omitting the division by g = 10 and halving.

stem: A 5 kg load is lifted 12 m above the ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², its gain in gravitational potential energy is
explanation: ΔPE = mgh = 5 × 10 × 12 = 600 J. Halving it (300 J) wrongly treats it like kinetic energy.

stem: At the highest point of its path, a projectile (no air resistance) has
options: zero horizontal velocity and acceleration g downwards
zero vertical velocity and acceleration g downwards
explanation: Only the vertical component vanishes at the top; the horizontal component stays constant. Gravity still acts, so the acceleration is g downwards all the time.

stem: One newton has the same unit as
options: the rate of change of momentum
the rate of change of energy
the product of mass and velocity
the product of pressure and volume
explanation: F = Δp/Δt, so force and momentum per second share the unit kg·m/s². Mass × velocity is momentum itself, pressure × volume is energy, and energy per second is power.

stem: A force is conservative if the work it does on a body moving between two points
options: is always equal to the change in momentum
is independent of the path taken
explanation: Gravity and the spring force are examples; friction is not, since its work depends on the path length.

stem: Two forces of 3 N and 4 N act on a body at right angles to each other. The magnitude of their resultant is
explanation: R = √(3² + 4²) = 5 N. The sum 7 N applies only when the forces act in the same direction.

stem: A 20 kg crate rests on a rough floor where the coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.4. Taking g = 10 m/s², the friction force while it slides is
explanation: f = μN = 0.4 × (20 × 10) = 80 N. 200 N is the weight, and 8 N results from using N = mg/g.

stem: In a perfectly inelastic collision between two bodies on a smooth surface, which quantity is conserved?
explanation: Momentum is conserved in every collision when no external force acts. Some kinetic energy is lost as heat and sound, and the bodies move off together.

stem: A 5 kg block slides down a smooth (frictionless) plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its acceleration is
explanation: Along the plane a = g sinθ = 10 × 0.5 = 5 m/s², independent of mass. g cosθ = 8.7 m/s² is the component perpendicular to the plane.

stem: A projectile is fired at 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its maximum height is
explanation: The vertical component is 20 sin30° = 10 m/s, so H = (10)²/(2 × 10) = 5 m. Using the full speed 20 m/s gives 20 m.

stem: A geostationary satellite has an orbital period of
explanation: It must complete one orbit in the time the Earth turns once so that it stays above the same point on the equator.

stem: A car moving at 20 m/s is brought to rest with a constant deceleration of 5 m/s². The stopping distance is
explanation: v² = u² + 2as gives 0 = 400 − 10s, so s = 40 m. 80 m comes from omitting the 2 in 2as.

stem: A car rounds a flat circular bend of radius 20 m. If the coefficient of friction between tyres and road is 0.5 and g = 10 m/s², the maximum safe speed is
explanation: Friction supplies the centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r, so v = √(μgr) = √(0.5 × 10 × 20) = √100 = 10 m/s. Forgetting the square root gives 100.

stem: Water flows at 2 m/s through a pipe of cross-section 4 cm². The pipe narrows to 1 cm². The speed of the water in the narrow part is
explanation: Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂, so v₂ = 4 × 2/1 = 8 m/s. 0.5 m/s results from inverting the area ratio.

stem: A stone is dropped from rest from a bridge. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its speed after 3 s?
explanation: v = u + gt = 0 + 10 × 3 = 30 m/s. 45 m is the distance fallen (½gt²), not a speed.

stem: The scalar product of two non-zero vectors is zero when the angle between them is
explanation: A·B = AB cosθ, which is zero only for θ = 90°. At 0° and 180° it takes its largest magnitudes, +AB and −AB.

stem: Archimedes' principle states that the upthrust on a body immersed in a fluid equals
options: the weight of the fluid displaced by the body
explanation: Upthrust is the weight of displaced fluid. It equals the body's weight only when the body floats freely.

stem: A projectile is fired at 20 m/s at 30° above the horizontal from level ground. Taking g = 10 m/s², its time of flight is
explanation: T = 2u sinθ/g = 2 × 20 × 0.5/10 = 2 s. Using cosθ instead gives about 3.5 s, and 1 s is only the time to the top.

stem: A block of volume 0.002 m³ is completely submerged in water (density 1,000 kg/m³). Taking g = 10 m/s², the buoyant force on it is
explanation: Buoyant force = ρVg = 1,000 × 0.002 × 10 = 20 N, the weight of water displaced. It does not depend on the block's own mass.

stem: A 2 kg mass is placed at x = 0 and a 3 kg mass at x = 5 m. The centre of mass lies at
explanation: x = (2 × 0 + 3 × 5)/(2 + 3) = 3 m, nearer the heavier mass. The midpoint 2.5 m is correct only for equal masses.

stem: An astronaut inside a satellite orbiting the Earth feels weightless because
options: there is no gravity at that height
the Earth's pull is cancelled by the Moon
the satellite is outside the atmosphere
she and the satellite are both in free fall with the same acceleration
explanation: Gravity is still strong at orbital heights; both fall towards the Earth with the same acceleration, so there is no contact force between them.

stem: The area under a force–time graph for a body represents
explanation: ∫F dt = impulse = change in momentum. The area under a force–distance graph is the work done.

stem: A small sphere falls through a viscous fluid. According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag on it, at low speed, is proportional to
options: its radius squared and its speed
its mass and the square of its speed
the square of its radius only
explanation: F = 6πηrv, so it varies linearly with both r and v. Drag proportional to v² is the model for fast turbulent motion.

stem: A uniform solid disc and a hoop of the same mass and radius are released together from rest at the top of a rough incline and roll without slipping. Which statement is correct?
options: The disc reaches the bottom first
The hoop reaches the bottom first
The result depends on their common mass
explanation: The hoop has a larger moment of inertia (mr²) than the disc (½mr²), so more of its energy goes into rotation and it accelerates less. Mass cancels out, so it does not affect the outcome.
